objective: Freeze what can and cannot be identified when observed institutional investor-class flow overlaps with passive/index/ETF mechanics, before any return outcome is opened.

newEvidence.source: Taiwan Stock Exchange Daily Trading Details of Foreign and Institutional Investors
newEvidence.implication: Official flow fields classify investor/desk categories such as foreign, investment trust, dealer proprietary and dealer hedge. They do not identify investment motive such as active conviction versus passive benchmark demand.

newEvidence.source: Taiwan Stock Exchange ETF creation/redemption overview
newEvidence.implication: ETF primary-market mechanics include in-kind and cash creation/redemption; PCF is a basket contract, not direct proof of same-day constituent execution.

newEvidence.source: Taiwan Stock Exchange ETF glossary and creation/redemption mechanics
newEvidence.implication: Minimum in-kind creation, aggregate creation and cash-in-lieu mean units-delta multiplied by PCF is modeled delivery exposure with execution uncertainty, not identified realized stock flow.

newEvidence.source: Yousefi, Najand and Sun (2024), Accounting & Finance, DOI 10.1111/acfi.13265
newEvidence.implication: Flow-performance evidence requires separating managerial/information interpretations from non-fundamental price pressure; positive flow-performance association alone does not identify smart money.

newEvidence.source: Brogaard, Heath and Huang (2026), Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis, ETF Sampling and Index Arbitrage
newEvidence.implication: ETF replication can sample indexes and channel arbitrage toward liquid stocks, so benchmark weights alone are not a sufficient execution model.

newEvidence.source: Xu (2025), Passive Flows, Index Rebalancing, and Price Impact
newEvidence.implication: Mechanical index-rebalancing demand can move prices without information, supporting a separate passive price-pressure mechanism.

newEvidence.source: Sammon and Shim (2026), Who Clears the Market When Passive Investors Trade?
newEvidence.implication: Other institutions may trade in the same direction as passive funds and firms can supply shares; therefore subtracting modeled passive demand from investor-class flow does not identify a clean active-conviction flow.

identificationFirewall.motiveState: ACTIVE_CONVICTION_UNIDENTIFIED unless an independent source identifies strategy/motive
identificationFirewall.passiveLayerRule: The three passive layers are not interchangeable and cannot be promoted into one another without direct evidence.
identificationFirewall.crowdingRule: D06-06 CORE_CROWDING consumes institutional/ownership/price-flow parents and is not an independent directional vote merely because it is a composite child.

preregisteredResidualQuestions.question: Does observed institutional flow retain incremental information after passive-event and modeled ETF basket controls plus price/volume, sector, liquidity and regime controls?
preregisteredResidualQuestions.null: No incremental contribution on common support.
preregisteredResidualQuestions.namingRule: Any residual is statistical residual flow, not active conviction.

preregisteredResidualQuestions.question: Does modeled passive ETF/index exposure retain incremental information after observed institutional flow and the same common controls?
preregisteredResidualQuestions.null: No incremental contribution on common support.
preregisteredResidualQuestions.namingRule: Modeled basket exposure is not actual passive execution.

preregisteredResidualQuestions.question: Does D06-06 crowding add incremental information beyond its exact parent receipts?
preregisteredResidualQuestions.namingRule: A transformed child does not create a second vote.

preregisteredResidualQuestions.question: Can an active-conviction interpretation be identified?
preregisteredResidualQuestions.null: UNIDENTIFIED absent a direct motive/strategy source or separately valid identification design.
preregisteredResidualQuestions.namingRule: Statistical residualization alone cannot pass this identity gate.

commonSupportRules: No zero-imputation for unavailable passive/flow parents.
Compare raw versus controlled/residual representations on the same observable rows.
Preserve source vintage and firstKnownAt for every parent.
Multiple symbols sharing one date or one rebalance event are not independent replications.
Multiple ETFs sharing one benchmark/event do not create independent event counts.
D16 must freeze horizon, benchmark, dependence handling, multiple-testing family and stop rule before outcomes open.
lineageRules: Every primitive carries primitiveReceiptId and informationRoot.
Expected index event, modeled ETF basket exposure and observed institutional flow may coexist but cannot be counted as three independent votes unless residual incrementality is proven.
D11 event identity and D06 passive-flow measurement share event lineage when they refer to the same rebalance episode.
D20 behavioral interpretation cannot create a new vote from the same D06 crowding/flow primitive without behavior-specific evidence.
